items.pronunciation_notes: यह is said 'ye', so the pair runs together as 'ye ghar' in ordinary speech.
items.gloss_en: a demonstrative standing before a noun

learn.explanation_en: A demonstrative can stand alone as the subject — यह अच्छा है — or it can sit in front of a noun and point at it. Once it modifies a noun, everything downstream has to follow: यह घर बड़ा है has four singular words in a row, and ये घर बड़े हैं has four plural ones. Notice that घर itself does not change in the plural, so the demonstrative, the adjective and the verb are carrying the number between them.

examples.note: Demonstrative, noun, adjective and verb all singular.
घर is unchanged, but everything around it is plural.
किताब is feminine, so नया takes its irregular feminine नई.

common_error.why_en: The adjective and the verb are plural, so the demonstrative has to be plural as well.

practice.question: ___ घर बड़े हैं।
practice.explanation_en: बड़े and हैं are both plural, so the demonstrative must be ये.

game.explanation_en: Only one option keeps the demonstrative, the adjective and the verb all plural together.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words are short and unstressed, and the नasal on हैं is a hum rather than a consonant.

learn.title_en: ये हैं — one person, spoken of with respect
learn.explanation_en: Hindi shows respect by using plural forms, and that applies to talking about someone as much as to talking to them. Anyone you would address as आप is referred to as ये or वे, with हैं, even though only one person is meant. So ये पिता जी हैं is 'this is my father', with a plural verb for a single man. It is the same machinery you met with आप — respect and plurality share their forms, and only the situation separates them.

examples.note: One person, plural forms throughout.
Respect again, and the same plural verb.
Or 'these are good' — only the situation decides which.

common_error.why_en: Respect uses plural forms all the way through, so the verb is हैं even for one person.

practice.question: ये पिता जी ___।
practice.explanation_en: जी marks respect, and respect takes plural forms — so हैं.

game.explanation_en: A respected person takes हैं. हो would need तुम as its subject.

items.pronunciation_notes: A flat ओ with no glide, so वो is one clean syllable and identical to how वह and वे are usually said.
items.gloss_en: the spoken form of वह and वे

learn.title_en: वो — what वह actually sounds like
learn.explanation_en: वह is written with a ह and said without one: in ordinary speech it comes out as वो. So does वे. That means the written singular and plural collapse into one spoken word, and you will also see वो written down in messages, subtitles and song lyrics. None of this is careless — it is simply what the language does. When listening, expect वो and let the verb tell you whether one thing or several are meant.

examples.note: Singular — and only the verb says so.
The same spoken word, now plural.
Written वह in careful spelling, वो in ordinary use.

common_error.why_en: If the verb is plural the adjective must be too. वो itself gives you no clue either way, so the rest of the sentence has to be consistent.

practice.question: वो अच्छे ___।
practice.explanation_en: अच्छे is plural, so the verb has to be हैं.

game.explanation_en: The adjective and the verb must match each other, since वो does not tell you the number.

summary.recap_en: This level finished the demonstratives. They can modify a noun or stand alone, they double as respectful singulars, and in speech वह and वे both come out as वो — which leaves the verb doing all the work of marking number.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the question words, and the second job that क्या does.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्य stack runs क straight into य with no vowel between them: kyaa, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: क्या asks about things. The important structural point is where it goes: in a Hindi question the question word sits where the answer would sit, not at the front as in English. यह क्या है? is literally 'this what is?'. That turns out to be easier than it sounds — build the statement first, then swap the unknown part for the question word, and leave the verb where it already was, at the end.

examples.note: क्या sits exactly where the answer will go.
The same shape, pointing further away.
Plural subject and plural verb, with क्या unchanged.

common_error.why_en: ये is plural, so the verb must be हैं. क्या itself never changes.

practice.question: ये क्या ___?
practice.explanation_en: ये is plural, so the verb is हैं.

game.explanation_en: यह is singular, so it takes है. ये would need हैं.

items.pronunciation_notes: As a question marker क्या is unstressed and often barely audible, with the rising tone carrying most of the work.
items.gloss_en: क्या as a yes-or-no question marker

learn.title_en: क्या at the front — a spoken question mark
learn.explanation_en: क्या has a second job, promised back in Module 4. Placed at the very front of a statement it turns the whole thing into a yes-or-no question and changes nothing else: चाय गरम है becomes क्या चाय गरम है?, 'is the tea hot?'. Here क्या means nothing at all by itself — it simply announces that a question is coming. In casual speech it is often dropped and a rising tone does the job instead.

examples.note: The statement is untouched; क्या is simply added at the front.
A yes-or-no question, not a 'what' question.
The same marker with a polite subject.

common_error.why_en: As a yes-or-no marker क्या belongs at the very front. Sitting in the middle it would be asking 'what' instead.

practice.question: ___ चाय गरम है?
practice.explanation_en: क्या at the front turns a statement into a yes-or-no question.

game.question_en: Which sentence means 'Is this a book?'
game.explanation_en: क्या at the front asks yes or no. In the middle it asks 'what', which gives a different question entirely.

items.pronunciation_notes: The open औ is a single vowel, nearer the aw of 'law' than the ow of 'cow': kaun.

learn.explanation_en: कौन asks about people, and it behaves exactly like क्या: it sits where the answer would go and the verb stays at the end. The one thing to watch is the verb. कौन can take either है or हैं depending on whether you expect one person or several — and because respect uses plural forms, a polite question about one person also takes हैं.

examples.note: One person expected, so है.
Genuinely plural, so हैं.
One person, asked respectfully — and so still हैं.

common_error.why_en: यह is singular, so the verb is है. The respectful version would use ये कौन हैं?

practice.question: यह कौन ___?
practice.explanation_en: यह is singular, so the verb is है.

game.explanation_en: वे is plural and takes हैं. The other three each pair a singular demonstrative with a plural verb or the reverse.

summary.recap_en: This level covered क्या and कौन. Hindi puts the question word where the answer would go rather than at the front — except when क्या leads the sentence, in which case it is asking yes or no rather than what.
summary.next_up_en: Next: कहाँ, कब and कैसे, and the relative of कैसे that does change form.

items.pronunciation_notes: The crescent nasalises the final vowel and adds no n sound: kahãa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: कहाँ asks about place and sits where the answer would go, like the others. It belongs to a set of three that end in the same nasalised vowel: कहाँ for where, यहाँ for here, वहाँ for there. Answering a कहाँ question in full usually needs a postposition — in the house, on the table — and those arrive in the next module, so for now the questions run ahead of the answers.

examples.note: The question word comes just before the verb.
The same shape in the past, with आप taking थे.
Singular subject, singular verb.

common_error.why_en: आप takes plural agreement, so its past form is थे and never था.

practice.question: आप कहाँ ___?
practice.explanation_en: आप takes plural agreement, so the past form is थे.

game.explanation_en: तुम takes हो. आप needs हैं or थे, and तू needs है.

items.pronunciation_notes: Unaspirated क with no puff of air, and the final vowel drops: kab, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: कब asks about time. With only होना available the questions it can form are limited — you can ask when something was or is, but most real 'when' questions need a full verb, which arrives in Module 7. The time words from the last module supply the answers: सुबह, शाम, रात, कल. कब और कहाँ? is a complete question with no verb in it at all.

examples.note: Asking about something in the past.
Asking about something still to come.
Two question words joined, with no verb needed.

common_error.why_en: वह is singular, so the past form is था. वे would take थे.

practice.question: वह कब ___?
practice.explanation_en: वह is masculine and singular, so the past form is था.

game.explanation_en: वह is singular and takes था. The other three all mismatch the subject and the verb.

items.pronunciation_notes: The open ऐ then a flat ए, with no glide on either: kaise, two syllables.

learn.title_en: कैसे — how, and कैसा — what kind
learn.explanation_en: कैसे asks how something is done, and in that sense it never changes. But it has a close relative that does change: कैसा asks what something is like, and it agrees like any -ा adjective — कैसा घर, कैसी किताब, कैसे बच्चे. This explains the greeting you have been using since level five. आप कैसे हैं? has कैसे because आप takes plural agreement, and a woman is asked आप कैसी हैं?

examples.note: Plural agreement with आप.
The familiar version, and still plural.
चाय is feminine, so the form becomes कैसी.

common_error.why_en: चाय is feminine, so the form has to agree with it just as an adjective would.

practice.question: चाय ___ है?
practice.explanation_en: चाय is feminine and singular, so the form is कैसी.

game.explanation_en: चाय is feminine and singular, so both the question word and the verb have to match it.

summary.recap_en: This level covered कहाँ, कब and कैसे. The first two never change form, but कैसे has a relative कैसा that agrees like an adjective — which is what the familiar greeting आप कैसे हैं? has been doing all along.
summary.next_up_en: Next: क्यों, and the two question words that agree with the noun.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्य stack plus a nasalised vowel, all in one syllable: kyoṁ.

learn.explanation_en: क्यों asks for a reason and never changes form. Answering it properly needs क्योंकि, meaning 'because', which arrives at the very end of this module — so for a while you will be able to ask why more easily than you can answer it. In the meantime क्यों नहीं?, 'why not?', is a complete and very usable question with no verb in it at all.

examples.note: The bare shape of the question.
A complete question with no verb.
आप takes थे in the past.

common_error.why_en: आप takes plural agreement, so the past form is थे.

practice.question: आप क्यों ___?
practice.explanation_en: आप always takes plural agreement, so the past form is थे.

game.explanation_en: वह is singular and takes था. आप needs थे, and तुम needs हो.

items.pronunciation_notes: The vowel before -ना drops, giving kitnaa in two syllables rather than three.

learn.title_en: कितना — how much, and it agrees
learn.explanation_en: कितना asks about quantity, and unlike every question word so far it changes form: कितना with a masculine singular, कितनी with a feminine, कितने with a masculine plural. It behaves exactly like बड़ा or अच्छा. That makes it the first question word where you have to know the gender of the noun before you can even ask about it — which is where the last module's 150 genders start earning their keep.

examples.note: पानी is masculine, so कितना — despite that -ी ending.
चाय is feminine, so कितनी.
Masculine plural, so कितने.

common_error.why_en: चाय is feminine, so कितना has to take its feminine form.

practice.question: ___ चाय?
practice.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, so the form is कितनी.

game.explanation_en: पानी is masculine and singular, so कितना. Its -ी ending is misleading, as it has been since Module 4.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two separate words, both unstressed, and सा carries the agreement rather than कौन.

learn.explanation_en: कौन on its own asks 'who'. Add सा and it becomes 'which', used to pick one item out of several. It is the सा part that agrees, not कौन: कौन सा घर, कौन सी किताब, कौन से बच्चे. English speakers regularly reach for कौन alone when they mean 'which', which asks about a person instead and lands strangely — कौन किताब? is close to asking 'who book?'.

examples.note: घर is masculine singular, so सा.
किताब is feminine, so सी.
Masculine plural, so से.

common_error.why_en: कौन alone asks 'who'. For 'which' you need सा, agreeing with the noun that follows.

practice.question: कौन ___ किताब?
practice.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, so सा becomes सी.

game.explanation_en: किताब is feminine and singular, so the form is सी. Dropping सा altogether changes the question to 'who'.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the question words. Most never change, but कितना and कौन सा agree with the noun exactly as adjectives do — so asking about quantity or choice requires knowing the gender first.
summary.next_up_en: Next: adjective agreement set out in full, and a conversation that shows all three forms at once.

items.pronunciation_notes: The च्छ stack pairs a plain च with an aspirated छ, so only the second half carries breath.

learn.explanation_en: An adjective ending in -ा takes three forms, decided by the noun it describes, and -ा itself is the masculine singular: अच्छा घर, बड़ा कमरा, नया कपड़ा. Adjectives that do not end in -ा — साफ़, गरम, खाली, सुंदर — never change at all, so this whole question only ever arises for the -ा group. When such an adjective appears in a sentence with होना, the verb agrees separately and both have to be right.

examples.note: घर is masculine and singular, so -ा.
The adjective and the verb agree separately with घर.
साफ़ never changes, so it tells you nothing about the gender.

common_error.why_en: घर is masculine, so the adjective takes -ा.

practice.question: यह घर ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: घर is masculine and singular, so the adjective takes -ा.

game.explanation_en: घर is masculine and singular, so the adjective is अच्छा.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ि matra on किताब is drawn before क but pronounced after it, as it has been since Module 3.

learn.explanation_en: -ी is the feminine form, and it covers both singular and plural: अच्छी किताब and अच्छी किताबें use exactly the same adjective. That is worth noticing, because it means a feminine plural shows its number in the noun and the verb but not in between. अच्छी किताबें हैं has a plural noun and a plural verb with an unchanged adjective sitting between them.

examples.note: किताब is feminine, so -ी.
Feminine plural, and the adjective does not change at all.
The adjective and the verb are both feminine.

common_error.why_en: Feminine adjectives keep -ी in the plural. Only masculine ones change to -े.

practice.question: ये किताबें ___ हैं।
practice.explanation_en: किताबें is feminine, and feminine adjectives keep -ी even in the plural.

game.explanation_en: किताबें is feminine plural, and the feminine adjective form does not change for number.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words end in a flat ए with no glide, so the phrase has a matched rhythm: achchhe bachche.
items.setting_en: Two neighbours talking about a family

learn.explanation_en: -े is the masculine plural: अच्छे बच्चे, बड़े घर, नए जूते. With this the set is complete — -ा for masculine singular, -ी for feminine of any number, -े for masculine plural. Listen for the switch in the exchange below: the neighbours move from a group of children to a single child, and the adjective and the verb both change together in the same breath.

common_error.why_en: बच्चे is masculine plural, so the adjective takes -े just as the verb takes हैं.

practice.question: वह बच्चा ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: बच्चा is masculine and singular here, so the adjective is अच्छा.

game.question_en: Listen to the second line. Which word is missing?
game.mask_reason: gender-marked adjective ending agreeing with बच्चे
game.explanation_en: बच्चे is masculine plural, so the adjective takes -े. The word itself is guessable; only the ending is in question.

summary.recap_en: This level set out adjective agreement in full: -ा for masculine singular, -ी for feminine of any number, -े for masculine plural, and no change at all for adjectives that do not end in -ा.
summary.next_up_en: Next: more on agreement, and then the postpositions that make longer sentences possible.
